title: ws.v1 — the public live WebSocket multiplex (/ws), frozen to vexa main
description: The /ws endpoint api-gateway serves: api_key auth (x-api-key header or ?api_key=), a subscribe/unsubscribe control protocol, and forwarded live data messages — transcript (the per-speaker confirmed/pending bundle) + transcription_segment from tc:meeting:{id}:mutable, meeting.status from bm:meeting:{id}:status, chat_message from va:meeting:{id}:chat. The gateway forwards the raw redis payload verbatim, so data messages are type-tagged and additive (extra fields allowed). Shapes are the canonical 0.10.6 contract (vexa-0.11 api-gateway + meetings.publish_meeting_status_change).

SubscribeRequest.description: client → server: subscribe to live updates for meetings

streams.description: optional, additive: which live streams to fan in. Absent = ["transcript"] (the 0.12 channels: transcript, meeting.status, chat_message). "signals" adds MeetingSignals for the row the authorize hop grants.

UnsubscribeRequest.description: client → server: stop receiving updates for meetings

Subscribed.description: server → client: ack of a subscribe (the meetings actually authorized + subscribed)

Unsubscribed.description: server → client: ack of an unsubscribe

TranscriptionSegment.description: server → client: a single live transcript segment (forwarded from tc:meeting:{id}:mutable). type + text are the floor; the producer adds speaker/timing/segment_id.

Transcript.description: server → client: the canonical 0.10.6 per-speaker transcript bundle (forwarded from tc:meeting:{id}:mutable) — `confirmed` (completed) + `pending` (in-progress) segment arrays for one speaker tick. This is what the collector publishes + the dashboard consumes live.

MeetingStatus.description: server → client: the canonical 0.10.6 meeting/bot status update (forwarded verbatim from bm:meeting:{id}:status). Status lives under `payload.status`; a `meeting` ref + `user_id` + `ts` are carried alongside (vexa-0.11 meetings.publish_meeting_status_change). Replaces the drifted `bot_status` frame.

ChatMessage.description: server → client: a chat message from the bot (forwarded from va:meeting:{id}:chat)

MeetingSignals.description: server → client: transcript signals for one meeting, from the redis stream sig:meeting:{id} (the signals service is its one writer), sent to a subscription that named streams:["signals"] — the newest entries first, then each new batch live. Same access as the transcript: the row the authorize hop granted. Each annotation scores one transcript segment against the meeting's listening brief: scores = {label: 0..1}, words = {word: significance 0..1}.

id.description: the stream entry id (a reconnect drops what it already has)

Notice.description: one stored notification row (#1783): who did what to which object, the text composed from those two names only, never content; `actions` are what it offers now (accept/decline a workspace invite, join/decline a call, open) and `state` what the person did with it (accepted, declined, joined).

Notification.description: server → client: something that happened to this person (#1783), forwarded from u:{user_id}:notifications — they were added to a chat or one was shared with them, mentioned, invited or added to a workspace, their invite was accepted or declined, a call started or a routine posted a run in a chat they are in, their own agent posted one line with `notify` (kind agent), a meeting was shared with them, or a bot was scheduled for or joined their meeting. The text names the actor and the object only, never content. Also stored: a client reads the unread ones on load (GET /agent/notifications).

NotificationUpdate.description: server → client: the person acted on a notification in some tab (POST /agent/notifications/act) — the row as it now is (read, its `state`, the `actions` it still offers) and the unread count; every tab replaces its copy.

NotificationRead.description: server → client: this person marked notifications read in some tab; every other tab updates its unread count (u:{user_id}:notifications).

Rail.description: server → client: a chat joined (added) or left (removed) this person's rail (u:{user_id}:notifications). Not stored: it tells the rail to read the chat list again now.

HomeItem.description: server → client: an item on this person's new-chat home moved (u:{user_id}:notifications, #1783) — prepared, live, replied, done… with the chat or page the work lives in. Not stored as a frame: the open home patches that card in place; a terminal state (replied, done) takes it off.

HomeComposed.description: server → client: a new home composition was appended for this person (u:{user_id}:notifications, #1783). The open home reads it again when the pointer is not on it, so nothing reorders under the cursor.

Error.description: server → client: a protocol/auth error. `error` is a fixed code from the vocabulary below (formalized as the enum on the property, so the conformance harness's emitted codes are machine-checked against this contract). Control/auth codes (exercised by the offline /ws conformance harness): missing_api_key, invalid_json, invalid_subscribe_payload, invalid_unsubscribe_payload, unknown_action. Downstream-auth codes — emitted by the deployed gateway's POST /ws/authorize-subscribe path (adapters.AdminApiAuthorizer), so they are PRODUCTION-ONLY and NOT reachable by the synchronous offline harness: authorization_service_error (downstream returned non-200; carries `status` + `detail`), authorization_call_failed (the downstream call raised; carries `details`). Connect-time codes: invalid_api_key (the key resolves to nobody, or is a worker delegation token; close 4401), auth_unavailable (the key could not be resolved now; close 4503), insufficient_scope (the key holds none of the scopes the REST routes for meeting status take — close 4403 — or, on a subscribe, none of the transcript read's; the socket stays open). Live re-authorization: subscription_revoked (an open meeting subscription that no longer passes POST /ws/authorize-subscribe — the owner removed the reader, turned a share off, or a workspace membership ended; carries `details` {platform, native_id}; that meeting's fan-in stops, the socket stays open).
